title: Find and remove the cause of the longer producer stage
summary: Investigate why the median producer stage per landed job grew from 12.7 to 23.5 minutes, using the stage-timing code in athena-core and the producer path. Fix the cause and write it down in a note under docs/design/. Audience: Athena maintainers reading the next throughput review.

defaults_applied.how: The fix and tests are in Rust.
cargo test and clippy must pass.
The criteria require fixing the cause, not the symptom.
The design note cites sources and labels estimates.
A test shows the behavior change.
The criteria tie to a lower producer median in the next review.
One focused change on the cause path.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (stage medians), crates/athena-core/src/store.rs and snapshot.rs (stage timing records), crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs (entry point and order of run stages), and crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (records validation allow-list). The change adds no new record or data file under crates/. If it does, it must be covered by check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test. Stage minutes are measured directly from recorded stage durations, not through a stand-in.

Assumption: the cause is in how the producer stage is run (for example cold builds, repeated checks inside the producer, oversized prompt or context, or retries). The producer must confirm it from the code and the recorded timings available to it before choosing a fix.
The rise in planning (1.7 to 9.0) may share the cause. A fix for it is out of scope unless it is the same root cause.
Producer wall time cannot be re-measured inside a verifier run. The verifier checks the mechanism by tests and the note's cited evidence.
Environment: none beyond the repository snapshot. No CI workflow, push or PR is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A note under docs/design/ states the cause of the longer producer stage. It cites the code paths and the measured numbers (12.7 to 23.5 minutes), and labels any estimate.
Run cargo test. A new or changed test fails on the old behavior and passes on the new, showing the identified cause no longer adds time to the producer stage.
Run cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check. Both are clean.
The diff touches only the code on the cause path and its tests. It does not change stage-median reporting merely to make the numbers look better.
The fix removes the cause itself, not a symptom such as a raised timeout or hidden timing. The note says what the next throughput review should show: a lower producer median.

out_of_scope: Changing the throughput review thresholds or the stage-median calculation
Fixing the planning, checks or verifier stage growth unless it shares the producer's root cause
Edits to athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows or prompt files
departures: The cause is unknown and must be found from timing data the producer may not fully see, so cost and verification risk are somewhat above the reference.
urgent_reason: It cuts wasted time: the producer stage takes about 10 more minutes per landed job than before.
hard_reason: This changes the run pipeline (how the producer stage is run and timed), so a mistake is costly and hard to see.
